Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
146 AM EDT Sat Sep 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 737 PM EDT Friday...Updated to decrease areal coverage and
intensity of fog tonight, as cyclonic flow will produce plenty
of clouds and limit fog development, except for parts of the CT
River Valley. Expecting low level stratus to develop after
midnight with higher terrain becoming obscured by morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 231 PM EDT Friday...

1. Isolated rain showers today and Saturday, then drier weather
Sunday and Monday. 

2. Stronger storm system for mid-late week followed by taste of
Fall.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 231 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: As upper level flow remains northwesterly over 
our region under an upper level trough we will have continued 
chances for isolated rain showers this afternoon and evening and
again on Saturday. Surface high pressure will ridge into our 
area from the north on Sunday and into Monday, leading to drier 
weather during that period. Will have areas of fog each 
overnight, highs generally in the 70s areawide.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The more dynamic fall-like synoptic pattern is 
beginning to become established. Going into mid and late week, a
deepening low will move east from Ontario into Quebec, with 
ensemble guidance indicating it will likely drop blow 990 mb by 
the time it reaches Atlantic Canada. The center of the low 
should pass by well to the north and the best dynamics should 
miss the region. While warm air advection will occur mid-week 
and bring a more humid airmass into the region, there will not 
be enough time for a fully tropical airmass to become 
established. Therefore, this will limit instability as the 
system passes by. During Wednesday night and into the day on 
Thursday, multiple boundaries/troughs/fronts will pass through 
and bring multiple rounds of showers. A favored nocturnal 
passage of the strongest dynamics and a marginal airmass should 
prevent a widespread severe threat, but with such a strong low 
to the north the threat will still be watched. Afterward, the 
coolest airmass of the season so far will become established, 
with widespread highs in the 60s (and potentially 50s in the 
cooler spots) for Friday. Depending on the position of the 
surface high over the weekend, first frost could be possible in 
the cold hollows.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...A mix of flight conditions is expected
across terminals over the next few hours, with lowering
ceilings and intermittent mist/fog making for variable
conditions. Ceilings are expected to trend MVFR over the next
few hours, generally by 09Z or so with some intervals of IFR
possible. KSLK and KMPV are most likely to see IFR conditions,
but it will also be possible at KBTV, KEFK, and KRUT generally
between 09Z and 13Z as as low level inversion develops. In
addition to ceilings, some visibility reductions will be
possible with some mist/fog developing, most likely at
KSLK/KMPV/KEFK. Ceilings are expected to improve to MVFR by 15Z
with a mix of MVFR/VFR by 18Z and all terminals trending VFR by
21Z. Winds will generally be light and variable overnight, with
northerly winds 5 to 10 knots expected for tomorrow afternoon
with some gusts of 20 knots or so possible. 

Outlook...

Sunday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Patchy BR.
Sunday Night: VFR. Patchy BR.
Labor Day: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Tuesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
